cues.zh: 我的车能感知到下雨。
cues.en: My car knows when it’s wet.

cues.zh: 没错，它有自动雨刷。
cues.en: That’s right, it’s got automatic windshield wipers.

cues.zh: 调到自动模式后，车一沾水，雨刷就动。
cues.en: When they’re set to automatic, and the car gets wet, they wipe.

cues.zh: 它怎么知道的？
cues.en: How it know that?

cues.zh: 其实很简单。
cues.en: It’s actually really simple.

cues.zh: 看挡风玻璃，
cues.en: If you look at the windshield,

cues.zh: 你会注意到顶部中央附近有一块黑色区域。
cues.en: you’ll notice an area near the top center which is black.

cues.zh: 再仔细看，就能看到车用来判断挡风玻璃干湿的元件。
cues.en: And if you look closelier you’ll see the component the car uses to determine windshield wetness.

cues.zh: 哦，是摄像头？
cues.en: Oh, the camera?

cues.zh: 不，不是摄像头——那就太蠢了！
cues.en: No, it's not the camera - that’d be silly!

cues.zh: 那样就得从本就极其复杂的计算机视觉任务中分出宝贵的时钟周期，
cues.en: Then you’d have to devote some precious clock cycles away from the already wildly complicated computer vision tasks

cues.zh: 而那些任务正帮助车辆保持在车道中央。
cues.en: which help keep the car centered in its lane.

cues.zh: 这决定看起来很奇怪，
cues.en: That seems like a weird decision

cues.zh: 而且不管堆多少软件更新，我都不知道这能有多靠谱。
cues.en: and I don’t even know how well that could possibly work no matter how many software updates you throw at it.

cues.zh: 不，我并没有特指什么，你为什么会这么想？
cues.en: No, I’m not alluding to anything specific, why on Earth would you think that?

cues.zh: 就在那个朝前看路面的摄像头正上方，你会看到一个小圆点，圆点里面还有一些小点，各位观众，
cues.en: Right above that camera which looks forward at the road you’ll see a little circular spot with some spots within the spot and that, viewers,

cues.zh: 那就是雨量传感器。
cues.en: is the rain sensor.

cues.zh: 瞧，我把它弄湿——车就刮起来了！
cues.en: Look, I get it wet - and the car wipes!

cues.zh: 但这一招我也会。
cues.en: But two can play at that game.

cues.zh: 你可能觉得这是极其复杂又昂贵的技术，
cues.en: You may think this is wildly complicated and expensive technology

cues.zh: 但其实它只是两个再简单不过的电子元件，以一种非常巧妙的方式协同工作。
cues.en: but actually it’s just two of the simplest electronic components you can imagine working together in a very clever way.

cues.zh: 雨量传感器的深色部分下方是红外LED，向上朝玻璃照射光线，
cues.en: Below the dark portions of the rain sensor are infrared LEDs shining light up into the glass,

cues.zh: 紧挨着它们的是检测这种光的光电二极管。
cues.en: and adjacent to them are photodiodes which detect that light.

cues.zh: 那底部那个亮点呢？
cues.en: Now, that bright spot at the bottom?

cues.zh: 它其实并不是雨量传感器的一部分。
cues.en: That’s not actually part of the rain sensor.

cues.zh: 这是一个用于自动控制汽车前灯的环境光传感器。
cues.en: It’s an ambient light sensor used to control the car’s headlights automatically.

cues.zh: 这两个组件只是位于同一个总成中。
cues.en: The two components just live in the same assembly.

cues.zh: 组成雨水传感器的部件其实并不太看得见
cues.en: The parts that make up the rain sensor aren’t really visible

cues.zh: 因为它们位于一个滤光片下方，该滤光片阻挡可见光，所以在我们眼中它看起来是黑色的。
cues.en: because they’re below a filter which blocks visible light and thus it appears black to our eyes.

cues.zh: 奇怪，我们不是刚在灶台上遇到过这种情况吗？
cues.en: That’s strange, didn’t we just encounter that with stovetops?

cues.zh: 最近总出现奇怪的关联。
cues.en: Weird connections happening lately.

cues.zh: 为了演示它如何检测雨水，我会用一块玻璃和一个激光笔。
cues.en: To demonstrate how that detects rain, I’ll use a piece of glass and a laser pointer.

cues.zh: 如果我把激光以大约45度角照向玻璃，
cues.en: If I shine the laser up at the glass at about a 45 degree angle,

cues.zh: 你会注意到一束激光点被反射回桌面方向。
cues.en: you’ll notice that a spot of laser light is reflected back down towards the table.

cues.zh: 我在那儿放一张纸，让它更明显。
cues.en: I’ll put a piece of paper there to make it more visible.

cues.zh: 现在看看我把玻璃弄湿时会发生什么。
cues.en: Now watch what happens when I get the glass wet.

cues.zh: 没什么大不了的。
cues.en: Not a whole lot.

cues.zh: 真可惜。
cues.en: That’s a bummer.

cues.zh: 啊，但这其实并不是雨水传感器原理的准确演示。
cues.en: Ah, but this isn’t actually an accurate demonstration of the principles involved in the rain sensor.

cues.zh: 与其看玻璃向下反射回来的光，
cues.en: Rather than look at the light reflected back downward by the glass,

cues.zh: 不如看看激光穿过玻璃后在上方形成的光斑。
cues.en: let’s look at the spot produced above the glass by the laser light which makes it through.

cues.zh: 现在仔细看。
cues.en: Now watch closely.

cues.zh: 看到了吗？它动了。
cues.en: Did you see that? It moved.

cues.zh: 这是因为玻璃上的水改变了光离开玻璃时的折射角。
cues.en: That happened because the water on top of the glass changed the angle of refraction as light left the glass.

cues.zh: 现在，像某些政客一样，我对光学这玩意儿真的不太在行，
cues.en: Now, like some politicians, I’m really not really good at the whole optics thing

cues.zh: 所以我就不深入细节了。
cues.en: so I’m not getting too deep into the weeds here.

cues.zh: 但当光从一种介质进入另一种介质时，它的速度其实会改变，
cues.en: But as light passes from one medium to another, its speed actually changes

cues.zh: 而由于……某些原因，这意味着它的方向看起来会发生变化。
cues.en: and because of… reasons that means it appears to change direction.

cues.zh: 这个概念叫做折射。
cues.en: That concept is known as refraction.

cues.zh: 水的折射率和空气的折射率不同。
cues.en: And the refraction index of water is different from that of air.

cues.zh: 这意味着光从玻璃进入空气和从玻璃进入水时，速度的变化不同，折射角的变化也不同。
cues.en: That means the change in speed and thus change in refraction angle is different between light passing from glass into air and light passing from glass into water.

cues.zh: 不过，雨水传感器完全位于玻璃下方，
cues.en: The rain sensor, though, is entirely under the glass

cues.zh: 所以它并不能直接检测到这种变化。
cues.en: so it’s not as if it can directly detect that change.

cues.zh: 相反，它利用的是全内反射效应。
cues.en: Instead, it leverages the effect of total internal reflection.

cues.zh: 如果你曾经戴着泳镜在泳池里游泳，并在水下抬头看水面，
cues.en: If you’ve ever gone swimming in a pool with goggles on and looked up at the surface of the water while submerged,

cues.zh: 你可能会注意到，从浅角度看去，它看起来像一面镜子。
cues.en: you may have noticed that it looks like a mirror from shallow angles.

cues.zh: 这里有一些素材片段来说明。
cues.en: Here’s some stock footage to illustrate.

cues.zh: 这就是全内反射在起作用——你正上方的水能很好地透光，你可以看穿它，
cues.en: That’s total internal reflection at work - the water directly above you transmits light just fine and you can see through it,

cues.zh: 但存在一个临界角，在这个角度下，空气-水界面会把所有光线全部反射回下方，
cues.en: but there’s a critical angle at which the air-water interface will reflect all light back down

cues.zh: 而且由于它像玻璃一样光滑，所以看起来就像一面镜子。
cues.en: and since it’s smooth like glass, it looks like a mirror.

cues.zh: 那么现在，雨量传感器如何利用这一点呢？
cues.en: So now - how can the rain sensor take advantage of that?

cues.zh: 首先，由于该模块并非玻璃的一部分，
cues.en: Well, first, since the module isn’t part of the glass,

cues.zh: 我们需要一种光学界面材料，将传感器与玻璃耦合起来，并消除底部玻璃与空气之间的光学界面。
cues.en: we need an optical interface material to couple the sensor to the glass and remove the air-to-glass optical interface on the bottom.

cues.zh: 这种材料是一种粘性凝胶，一旦就位，你就看不见它了。
cues.en: That takes the form of a sticky gel which, now that it’s in-place, you can’t see.

cues.zh: 而这其实正是关键所在——当它发挥作用时，
cues.en: Which, really, is the point - when it’s doing its job,

cues.zh: 传感器和玻璃就合为一体
cues.en: the sensor and the glass become one

cues.zh: （从光学角度来看）。
cues.en: (from an optical perspective).

cues.zh: 关键在于，我们之前提到的红外LED
cues.en: Now the key is that the infrared LEDs that we talked about earlier

cues.zh: 是以略小于全内反射临界角的角度向上照射玻璃的。
cues.en: are shining up at the glass just shallow of the critical angle of total internal reflection.

cues.zh: 因此，它们产生的所有光线都会直接从玻璃顶面反射回来，向下行进。
cues.en: So, all the light they produce will simply bounce off the top surface of the the glass and head back downward.

cues.zh: 而在那束光的另一端，是一个光电二极管。
cues.en: And, at the other end of that beam of light, is a photodiode.

cues.zh: 它会检测 LED 发出的光。
cues.en: That will then detect the light being generated by the LED.

cues.zh: 为了确保它检测到的是那束光而不是别的东西，
cues.en: And to make sure it’s detecting that light and not something else,

cues.zh: LED 实际上在快速闪烁，而光电二极管在寻找那种闪烁模式。
cues.en: the LEDs are actually rapidly blinking and the photodiode is looking for that pattern of blinks.

cues.zh: 简单来说，就是 LED 在产生一种特定的调制信号，而光电二极管被调谐来检测它。
cues.en: That’s a simpler way of saying the LEDs are producing a specific modulated signal that the photodiode is tuned to detect.

cues.zh: 但因为光电二极管和 LED 之间的角度非常接近全内反射的临界角，
cues.en: But because the angle between the photodiode and the LED is so close to the critical angle of total internal reflection,

cues.zh: 如果条件发生变化，光电二极管接收到的信号强度也会随之改变。
cues.en: if conditions should change the intensity of that signal being received by the photodiode will also change.

cues.zh: 什么条件？
cues.en: What condition?

cues.zh: 潮湿的条件。
cues.en: Condition wet.

cues.zh: 玻璃上有水，正如我们在前面的演示中看到的，会改变折射角，因为水的折射率与空气不同。
cues.en: Water on the glass, as we saw in the earlier demo, changes the refraction angle because its refractive index is different from air.

cues.zh: 它会改变得恰到好处，足以破坏全内反射的效果。
cues.en: And it will change it just enough to break the effect of total internal reflection.

cues.zh: 湿润的玻璃会让 LED 产生的一部分光实际逃逸出去，并透射到外表面。
cues.en: Wet glass will allow some of the light produced by the LEDs to actually escape and be transmitted through to the outside surface.

cues.zh: 这反过来意味着，向下反射到光电二极管被检测到的光就更少了，
cues.en: Which in turn means there’s less light bouncing down to the photodiode to be detected,

cues.zh: 于是它接收到的信号开始减弱。
cues.en: so the signal it was receiving begins to diminish.

cues.zh: 而且，借助一点逻辑电路和编程，你就可以把这种信号损失用作挡风玻璃湿度的测量。
cues.en: And, with a little logic circuitry and programming, you can use that loss of signal as a measurement of windshield wetness.

cues.zh: 说实话……就是这么简单！
cues.en: And honestly… that’s it!

cues.zh: 就是这么简单。
cues.en: It’s that simple.

cues.zh: 传感器开始察觉到来自 LED 的信号下降，于是它就对挡风玻璃雨刮电机说——
cues.en: The sensor starts to see the signal from the LED drop out so it says to the windshield wiper motor -

cues.zh: 刮。
cues.en: wipe.

cues.zh: 玻璃越湿，信号下降得越多，所以刮得也越频繁。
cues.en: And the wetter the glass, the more the signal drops, so the more it wipes.

cues.zh: 而且你会注意到，传感器被特意放在雨刮器的路径上，这样每次刮动都能清洁玻璃。
cues.en: And you’ll notice the sensor is deliberately placed in the path of the windshield wipers so they clear the glass with every wipe.

cues.zh: 这样一来，逻辑就能根据每次擦拭后信号下降的速度，大致判断雨下得有多大。
cues.en: That allows the logic to get some sense of how hard it might be raining based on how quickly the signal drops out after every wiping event.

cues.zh: 这里唯一的另一个复杂点就是校准。
cues.en: The only other complexity here is calibration.

cues.zh: 每次传感器上电时，都得选一个它认为“干燥”的基线信号水平。
cues.en: Every time the sensor powers up, it’s got to pick a baseline signal level which it deems “dry.”

cues.zh: 不过，如果你正在外面淋着雨，发动汽车时挡风玻璃已经湿了，
cues.en: Yet, if you are out and about in the rain and you turn your car on with the windshield already wet,

cues.zh: 它起步时的信号水平就会比通常低一些。
cues.en: it’s going to start out with some lower signal level than typical.

cues.zh: 所以，大概有比我聪明的人设定了一个最低信号下降阈值，只要达到就一定会触发擦拭，
cues.en: So, somebody smarter than me probably established a minimum signal dropout level which always causes a wipe,

cues.zh: 事实上我很确定自己遇到过车子在启动后立刻擦了一次，
cues.en: and in fact I’m certain I’ve encountered the car do a single wipe after turning it on

cues.zh: 而当时其实并不怎么需要擦。
cues.en: when it didn’t really need to.

cues.zh: 但擦过之后，它就能重新校准了。
cues.en: But then it can reset its calibration after that wiping event.

cues.zh: 它还有个绝招，也是我最喜欢的一个：
cues.en: And, there’s another trick up its sleeve, and it's my very favorite one:

cues.zh: 就是装两个。
cues.en: having two of them.

cues.zh: 这里其实有两个传感器组件。
cues.en: There are actually two sensor assemblies under here.

cues.zh: 用手机摄像头拍出来，能勉强看到红外光。
cues.en: You can barely make out the infrared light in this smartphone camera footage.

cues.zh: 你会看到有两个光点。
cues.en: You'll see there's two spots.

cues.zh: 如果挡风玻璃是干的，两个传感器应该看到非常相似的信号
cues.en: If the windshield is dry, the two sensors should see very similar signals

cues.zh: 但只要其中一个上面有一丁点水，或者两个上面的水量不同，
cues.en: but if there’s even just a tiny bit of water on top of one of them, or differing amounts between the two,

cues.zh: 那两个信号就会差别很大，它立刻就知道挡风玻璃湿了。
cues.en: then the two signals will be very different and it will know immediately that the windshield is wet.

cues.zh: 它实际用的是哪种校准方法？
cues.en: Which calibration method is it actually using?

cues.zh: 我不知道。
cues.en: I do not know.

cues.zh: 如果你从没开过带自动雨刷的车，可能想知道：它们很好用，但也不是完美无缺。
cues.en: And if you’ve never lived with a car with automatic wipers, you may wish to know they are great but not exactly perfect.

cues.zh: 雨刷拨杆上有灵敏度调节功能，你可以按自己的喜好微调它的行为。
cues.en: You are afforded a sensitivity adjustment on the wiper stalk, so you can fine-tune its behavior to your liking.

cues.zh: 但虽然雨刷基本上总能在需要时启动，
cues.en: But while the wipers pretty much always come on when they need to,

cues.zh: 有时候明明只是毛毛雨，它们却疯狂乱刷；或者突然下起倾盆大雨，它们又有点偷懒。
cues.en: sometimes they go absolutely nuts when it’s barely raining or they get a little lazy in a sudden downpour.

cues.zh: 幸运的是，遇到这种情况，我只需拍一下方向盘旁的这个拨杆，
cues.en: Lucky for me, if that happens all I have to do is just slap this stalk which is right next to my hand on the steering wheel

cues.zh: 雨刷就会全速启动！
cues.en: and the wipers will come on full-steam!

cues.zh: 拨杆这用户界面真方便。
cues.en: Handy user interface, those stalks.

cues.zh: 它们总是在那儿，肌肉记忆自然接管！
cues.en: They’re always there and muscle memory takes over!

cues.zh: 我是支持拨杆的，这就是我的意思。这是个好设计。
cues.en: I’m pro-stalks, is what I’m saying. It’s a good idea.

cues.zh: 不过，没那么好的设计是，我为了换雨刷片，不得不去查的那个类似科乐美秘技的操作。
cues.en: What’s less of a good idea, though, is the Konami-code like trick I had to look up just to change my car’s wiper blades.

cues.zh: 引擎盖挡住你，让你没法抬起雨刮臂，所以你需要让它们停在上方位置才能更换。
cues.en: The hood blocks you from lifting the wiper arms so you need them to stop in the up position in order to change them.

cues.zh: 尽管我翻遍了所有设置菜单，也没找到“更换雨刮”这个选项。
cues.en: and despite digging through all the settings menus I couldn’t find a “change wipers” option.

cues.zh: 于是我试着在雨刮处于上方位置时直接关掉车，你知道，就是掐准时机按电源键，
cues.en: So I tried just switching the car off with the wipers in the up position, y'know just time it right, using the power button,

cues.zh: 但它比我聪明，还是把雨刮归位了。
cues.en: but it outsmarted me and parked them anyway.

cues.zh: 原来你得先关掉车，然后把雨刮拨杆按到喷水位置保持几秒，
cues.en: It turns out what you have to do is turn the car off and then hold the wiper stalk up in the mist position for a few moments

cues.zh: 然后车就会这样。
cues.en: and then the car will do this.

cues.zh: 这个流程在车主手册里有吗？
cues.en: Is this procedure in the owner’s manual?

cues.zh: 有，但谁会去那儿找信息啊？
cues.en: Yes, but who looks there for information?

cues.zh: 我通常喜欢用类似寓意的东西来结束视频。
cues.en: I usually like to end my videos with something akin to a moral.

cues.zh: 本着这个思路，今天的第一个教训是给我自己的，
cues.en: In that vein, the first lesson today is for me

cues.zh: 那就是去读那本该死的手册！
cues.en: and that is to read the freaking manual!

cues.zh: 这里面甚至还有个索引，找到合适的信息本来只需片刻。
cues.en: There’s even an index in here and finding the appropriate information would have taken me mere moments.

cues.zh: 人们在这上面花了很多心血，而我却……完全无视了它！
cues.en: People worked hard on this thing and I just… completely ignored it!

cues.zh: 所以，别忽视你生活中的那些手册。
cues.en: So don’t ignore the manuals in your life.

cues.zh: 第二个教训是……
cues.en: And the second moral is…

cues.zh: 别忽视用几个简单组件就能做到的事。
cues.en: don’t ignore what you can do with a few simple components.

cues.zh: 软件不是一切。
cues.en: Software isn’t everything.

cues.zh: 这可不是针对某个特定组织说的，别多心。
cues.en: That’s not directed at any organization in particular, mind you.

cues.zh: 只是记在心里就好。
cues.en: Just something to keep in mind.

cues.zh: 我讲到10分钟了吗？
cues.en: Did I get to 10 minutes yet?

cues.zh: ♫ 内心播放平滑爵士乐 ♫
cues.en: ♫ internally smooth jazz ♫

cues.zh: 顺便感谢Patreon上的支持者Jason推荐了这个视频主题。
cues.en: Thanks, by the way, to Jason, a supporter on Patreon, for recommending this video topic.

cues.zh: 那是很久以前的事了，而且我很确定这期间至少还有另一个人提过这个建议。
cues.en: That happened a long time ago and I’m pretty certain at least one other person has suggested this in the meantime

cues.zh: 所以如果我忘了你是谁，抱歉。
cues.en: so if I forgot who you were, I’m sorry.

cues.zh: 太多双金属片挡路了。
cues.en: There’s just too many bimetallic strips getting in the way.

cues.zh: 没错，它带自动……这东西没启动。
cues.en: That’s right, it’s got automatic… the thing didn’t start.

cues.zh: 你会注意到激光光点是……哦。
cues.en: You’ll notice that the spot of laser light is re… oh.

cues.zh: ……条件应该改变，强度……
cues.en: …conditions should change, the intensity of a-

cues.zh: 哦，我得加个逗号才行
cues.en: Ooh, I needed a comma for my sake

cues.zh: ……全内反射的临界角
cues.en: ...critical angle of total internal reflection

cues.zh: ……它得选一个基线信号杆。
cues.en: ...it’s got to pick a baseline signal lever.

cues.zh: 信号。
cues.en: Signal.

cues.zh: 电平。
cues.en: Level.

cues.zh: ……得看看，哦对，我忘了，哦对，我得拿那东西！
cues.en: ...had to look, oh yeah I forgo ohyeahIgottagetthething!

cues.zh: 你是说，只需要一个 LED、一个光电二极管和一点胶水，就能把检测雨水的任务从复杂的计算机视觉系统里拿走？
cues.en: You mean to say all you need is an LED, a photodiode, and a bit of adhesive to take the task of detecting rain away from a sophisticated computer vision system?

cues.zh: 而且这还是九十年代就有的技术？
cues.en: And that this was a technology available back in the nineties?

cues.zh: 这听起来不可能啊，我是说，要是真有更好的办法，那肯定只会出自某一家公司的殿堂，而不是别人。
cues.en: That sounds unpossible, I mean if there were a better way to do things, surely it would only come from the halls of one particular company and not anyone else.

cues.zh: 这一节通常是用来玩双关的，但今天我选了恶毒讽刺。
cues.en: This section is usually for puns but today I chose vicious sarcasm.

cues.zh: 当然，不是针对任何特定组织 :)
cues.en: Not directed at any particular organization, of course :)
